security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown, security examples, or defensive reference material and are false positives. The CI asset contains a confirmed critical supply-chain risk because it pipes an unpinned remote installer directly to Bash.

remediation.issue: The tfsec installation step executes a remote script from a mutable branch without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Install a pinned tfsec release from a trusted package or verify a pinned artifact checksum before execution.

content.value_statement: Security skill authors need consistent workflows, references, and validation patterns. This template provides reusable structures for security guidance, rules, and CI scanning.
actual_capabilities: Structures a security skill with discovery metadata, workflows, resources, integrations, troubleshooting, and references.
Provides sequential, conditional, iterative, feedback-loop, and incident-response workflow patterns.
Supplies example security rules mapped to OWASP, CWE, MITRE ATT&CK, and compliance standards.
Provides a GitHub Actions template for SAST, dependency, secret, container, and infrastructure scanning.
Demonstrates vulnerable and remediated patterns for SQL injection, XSS, credentials, cryptography, authentication, passwords, and file uploads.
limitations: The skill is a generic scaffold and still contains placeholder names, commands, links, and metadata.
The referenced example scripts are not included in the bundled files.
Security rules and CI settings require adaptation and validation for each repository and toolchain.
The CI template includes an unsafe remote installer that must be replaced before use.

use_cases.title: Create an application security skill
use_cases.description: Define repeatable vulnerability analysis, severity classification, remediation, and validation steps for a development team.

use_cases.title: Standardize DevSecOps scanning
use_cases.description: Adapt the CI asset to document approved scanners, artifacts, thresholds, and reporting practices.

use_cases.title: Document incident workflows
use_cases.description: Use the checklist patterns to structure detection, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a security skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a security skill outline for [security task]. Define users, triggers, workflow steps, expected outputs, and validation criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new security skill

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a security rule
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the rule template for [vulnerability]. Include detection logic, severity, framework mappings, vulnerable examples, safe alternatives, and false-positive guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI security workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the CI template for [repository stack]. Select scanners, pin trusted dependencies, define permissions, set failure thresholds, and retain useful artifacts.

prompt_templates.title: Build a validated response workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an incident-response skill for [incident type]. Include decision branches, approvals, evidence handling, containment checks, recovery validation, escalation, and audit outputs.

output_examples.input: Create a SAST skill outline for Python services.
output: Purpose: Identify exploitable Python code patterns and provide verified remediation.
Workflow: Scope the repository, run approved analysis, classify findings, propose fixes, validate changes, and document residual risk.
Validation: Re-run focused tests and the configured scanner before reporting completion.

output_examples.input: Plan CI security scanning for a Node.js repository.
output: Checks: Static analysis, dependency audit, secret detection, and container scanning.
Controls: Minimal permissions, pinned actions, verified tool installation, explicit thresholds, and retained reports.
Reporting: Publish concise findings and preserve detailed artifacts for authorized reviewers.

best_practices: Replace every placeholder and verify each referenced resource before publishing the skill.
Pin executable dependencies and grant CI jobs only the permissions required for their tasks.
Validate generated rules and workflows against representative repositories before operational use.
anti_patterns: Do not execute remote installers directly from mutable branches.
Do not present vulnerable examples without clear labels and nearby remediation.
Do not claim tool support, scripts, or integrations that are absent from the package.

faq.question: Is this a ready-to-run security skill?
faq.answer: No. It is a scaffold with placeholders and examples that require adaptation and validation.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the package include executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. SKILL.md references example scripts, but the scanned package does not include them.

faq.question: Which security frameworks are represented?
faq.answer: The examples reference OWASP, CWE, MITRE ATT&CK, NIST, SOC 2, PCI DSS, and GDPR.

faq.question: Can I use the CI template without changes?
faq.answer: No. Replace the remote pipe-to-shell installer, pin dependencies, review permissions, and adapt scanners for your repository.

faq.question: What outputs can the template help define?
faq.answer: It can structure findings, remediation guidance, validation results, security reports, workflow checklists, and retained scan artifacts.
